title: Land rights groups make 33 demands; adviser cites Tk 2,500 farm card
excerpt: Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir told an ALRD and ANGOC conference that a Tk 2,500 farm card for poor farmers will end food insecurity.
content:
The government has introduced a farm card giving poor farmers Tk 2,500 to buy agricultural inputs, which will end food insecurity, Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, Finance and Planning Adviser to the Prime Minister, said, Bonik Barta reported. He joined online on the closing day of a two-day international conference on 17 November. He also said the government had started digging 20,000 km of canals and rivers.

The conference, on responsible land governance and food sovereignty for climate-affected marginalised communities, was hosted by the Association for Land Reform and Development (ALRD) and the Asian NGO Coalition for Agrarian Reform and Rural Development (ANGOC). Civil society groups made 33 recommendations.

In a session chaired by Mahin Sultan, senior fellow of practice at BRAC, speakers from Bangladesh, India, Indonesia and Nepal said laws protecting smallholders, women and Indigenous peoples exist but are poorly implemented, and some contain discriminatory provisions. Other participants included Khushi Kabir, chairperson of ALRD; Shamsul Huda, executive director of ALRD; Sabine Lauber, chief of mission of OHCHR; and Syeda Rizwana Hasan, chief executive of BELA, the paper reported.

Why it matters

Land is at the root of poverty and climate displacement for many of the households NGOs work with. The farm card is a new channel of support, and the conference set out an advocacy agenda for land and food rights groups.

What to watch

Who qualifies for the farm card and how it is distributed, and whether the 33 recommendations are taken up by the ministries.
